paragraphs: In [Avodah Zarah 16a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.16a.12): Rav Ashi said, “Zevida (an [animal fattener](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.16a.12.3)) told me: ‘We keep a young ox, and it does the work of two.’” Hyman does not count him among the Torah scholars.

notes.text: [Rashi’s gloss](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.16a.12.5) compares the work of the ox with that of other oxen.
The context is whether an ox kept for fattening may regain strength and be used to work. Hyman’s comment about Zevida’s standing remains his own.

Hyman’s print (vol. I, p. 382) gives the heading Zevida and cites Avodah Zarah 16a. Rashi describes Zevida as an animal fattener and explains the comparison as one with other oxen. The passage asks whether the ox regains strength and can work. The young ox does twice the work of other oxen. Hyman gives the classification about Torah scholars.
